text:
sara: FYI I'm seeing a weird flake in our Android 15 sample app — long-running streaming calls eventually fail with repeated 504s after a token refresh. Repro is pretty reliable on device.

tom_b: ugh. is this the auth refresh that blocks the interceptor thread?

sara: yeah looks like. stack shows okhttp's Dispatcher queues getting backed up, lots of calls stuck in WAITING_FOR_RESPONSE.

chris_ml: can you paste the okhttp client config? specifically dispatcher, connectionPool, timeouts?

sara: here, simplified:
```kotlin
val dispatcher = Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 5 }
val pool = ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(pool)
  .dispatcher(dispatcher)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .callTimeout(120, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```

rahul: and AuthInterceptor does synchronous refresh? that will block the calling thread, could deadlock if refresh makes an API call through same client.

sara: yep. AuthInterceptor does a blocking refresh synchronized on tokenLock and then retries original request. Refresh calls the token endpoint using retrofit (same client).

tom_b: classic reentrancy problem. OkHttp docs: don't call the same client from an interceptor/Authenticator. Use a separate client for token requests (no interceptors) or use Authenticator which runs on a dedicated thread.

chris_ml: we also saw keepalive+connection reuse making it worse on Android 15 — pooled connections get reused for the refresh attempt and then the blocked call prevents pool eviction, so backlog grows.

sara: logs: many entries like `Http2Connection$Stream.reset: streamId=... CANCEL` then `Dispatcher: queued calls: 52 running: 12`. Eventually requests get 504 or stream timeout.

rahul: two practical fixes: 1) make token refresh use a separate NoAuth OkHttpClient with small dispatcher (so it doesn't consume app pool), 2) move refresh into an Authenticator (OkHttp's Authenticator is called on network loop and can synchronously return challenge) — but Authenticator still must not re-enter the same client.

tom_b: also consider lowering callTimeout or using per-route dispatcher config (not exposed easily). For mobile we prefer smaller connection pool and lower maxRequestsPerHost so single tenant doesn't starve.

sara: tried separate client trick and it fixed the repro locally. But we need an SDK example that demonstrates safe pattern. Current sample app uses single client which is bad.

chris_ml: agree — sample app should show: 
- interceptor only attaches auth header if token present
- if 401 -> do NOT call blocking refresh from interceptor; instead signal and use a refresh client, or use OkHttp Authenticator with separate client
- set retryOnConnectionFailure=false for streaming endpoints

rahul: small note: Android 15 changed some HTTP/2 prioritization behavior, so connection reuse edge cases surfaced more frequently than on older OS. Worth calling out in the sample README.

sara: I'll open a PR to update sample app to use a separate refresh client + add a test that simulates blocked refresh. Also propose adding a short diag in SDK docs about "do not call same client from interceptor".

tom_b: sg. can you include a small gist of the fix? I can add to the SDK migration guide.

ci-bot: build/24123 triggered by sara/retrofit-auth-fix; running unit tests.

sara: thanks — pinging once PR is up. If anyone has a better repro harness for Android 15 networking oddities, please share. :pray:
